5. Verdict

  • Imitation (Task A). HGB-truth reaches balanced accuracy 0.949 on test and 0.887 on stress (test_ood); HGB-sensor, the deployed model, 0.760 / 0.796 (switch F1 0.841 on test). The gap between the two is the price of not observing moving vehicles and arrivals; the teacher is a rule of n_*, which no loop detector delivers.
  • Queue forecast (Task B). HGB MAE 2.56 veh on test vs 3.68 veh for the naive ‘queue now’ baseline (R^2 0.989); on stress 4.22 vs 5.92. The action effect in the partial dependence is -0.61 veh (best other action minus hold), small against the state effect.
  • Acceptance bound, design, noise 0: 0/8 seeds pass (pass rate 0.00); mean ratio 1.272 [1.251, 1.293] (car delay 91.3 s vs 71.8 s). The bound is NOT met on every seed. Methodology form: paired difference +19.5 s, 95% upper end +20.8 s against a margin of 7.2 s: NOT met.
  • Acceptance bound, high, noise 0: 8/8 seeds pass (pass rate 1.00); mean ratio 1.014 [0.971, 1.056] (car delay 338.7 s vs 333.6 s). The bound is met on every seed and the interval lies below 1.10. Methodology form: paired difference +5.1 s, 95% upper end +19.5 s against a margin of 33.4 s: met.
  • Acceptance bound, pooled over demand levels, noise 0: pass rate 0.50 (8/16), mean ratio 1.143 [1.069, 1.217].
  • Acceptance bound, design, noise 0.1: 0/8 seeds pass, mean ratio 1.324 [1.299, 1.349].
  • Acceptance bound, high, noise 0.1: 8/8 seeds pass, mean ratio 0.954 [0.906, 1.002].
  • design: on ambulance delay the ML controller beats max_pressure (-44.2 +- 4.6 s); on car delay it loses to max_pressure (+19.5 +- 1.3 s). Against its own teacher priority_mp the ML controller’s ambulance delay differs by -0.6 s (mean over seeds). The teacher itself changes ambulance delay by -43.5 +- 4.6 s and naive preemption by -49.6 +- 5.0 s versus max_pressure.
    • car delay penalty of the ambulances: ML does not differ significantly from max_pressure (-0.178 +- 3.447; ML 1.858 vs 2.036).
    • recovery time: ML does not differ significantly from max_pressure (+5.801 +- 32.253; ML 60.440 vs 54.639).
    • fairness ratio: ML does not differ significantly from max_pressure (-0.001 +- 0.032; ML 1.127 vs 1.128).
  • high: on ambulance delay the ML controller beats max_pressure (-165.9 +- 21.2 s); on car delay it does not differ significantly from max_pressure (+5.1 +- 14.4 s). Against its own teacher priority_mp the ML controller’s ambulance delay differs by -34.0 s (mean over seeds). The teacher itself changes ambulance delay by -131.9 +- 17.9 s and naive preemption by -207.0 +- 29.5 s versus max_pressure.
    • car delay penalty of the ambulances: ML does not differ significantly from max_pressure (+8.088 +- 16.386; ML 23.890 vs 15.801).
    • recovery time: ML beats max_pressure (-64.549 +- 47.062; ML 62.031 vs 126.580).
    • fairness ratio: ML does not differ significantly from max_pressure (+0.160 +- 0.211; ML 1.369 vs 1.208).
  • Reference check, high: plain fixed_time beats max_pressure on car delay (-178.1 +- 25.2 s, throughput +373 +- 40 veh/h). The max-pressure rule as specified for this simulator (split phasing, one-approach pressure, 2-vehicle hysteresis) is therefore not a strong baseline at this demand; the ML controller imitates a teacher built on that rule and inherits the weakness. This is a finding about the simulator’s controllers, reported as is.
  • Agreement. Deployed, the ML controller’s request equals the teacher’s on 69.0% of main-period decision instants (mean over its episodes at noise 0); the residual disagreement is concentrated on hysteresis-boundary and max-green rows and on ambulance rows, where the sensor set cannot see n_*.
  • Safety. 0 invariant violations in 224 closed-loop episodes: the signal plant, not the model, guarantees safety.
  • Scope. All of this is one simulator with its own teacher rule and calibrated demand; the closed-loop seeds are disjoint from training but the demand model, OD pattern and vehicle population are the same as in training. Nothing here is evidence about a real junction.

6. Reproducibility

  • Simulator: traffic_twin_v1.2, config hash ecd36a4b3cad; dataset traffic_twin_v1.2, config hash ecd36a4b3cad, 120 episodes.
  • Software at evaluation time: Python 3.13.2, numpy 2.2.6, pandas 2.3.3, scikit-learn 1.7.2, joblib 1.5.2; macOS-15.2-arm64-arm-64bit-Mach-O.
  • Supervised pipeline: 563 s; scikit-learn 1.7.2, dataset config hash ecd36a4b3cad.
  • Closed loop: 352 s, 8 workers, seeds 900001..900008, hysteresis margin 0.1, noise variant 0.1.
  • Every number in this report is computed from the stored per-episode results; the report can be rebuilt without re-simulating.

12.6 Standard for Data Science Process, Data Governance and Management

  • Process standard. The CRISP-DM phases (Chapman et al., 2000) map onto the milestones: business understanding (proposal), data understanding (validation and data card), data preparation (generator, flags, splits), modelling (tasks A and B), evaluation (closed loop on paired seeds), deployment (offline replay of a logged episode, the first digital-twin step of Section 13). Code follows PEP 8 (van Rossum et al., 2001) with unit tests and a semantic generator_version.
  • Data standards. FAIR (Wilkinson et al., 2016): findable (download link, data card), accessible (CSV), interoperable (SI units, data dictionary with namespaces), reusable (licence, configuration and seed regenerate any row). The data card follows the datasheets-for-datasets pattern (Gebru et al., 2021). Quality dimensions: completeness (conservation invariant), consistency (label recompute test), accuracy (validation experiments).
  • Accessibility. Public download link (12.4), CSV readable by any tool, data dictionary and data card alongside, versioned releases named by generator_version and config_hash; any row can be regenerated from the configuration and the seed, so the data never depend on one hosting location.
  • Security and integrity. SHA-256 checksums published with the link; code and data under version control; a corrupted or altered copy is detected by the checksum and rebuilt from the seed rather than trusted. Retention as versioned releases.
  • Confidentiality. The dataset is synthetic: no personal data, no consent issues, no re-identification risk. Provenance is (generator version, configuration hash, seed). Proposed licences: CC BY 4.0 for data, MIT for code.
  • What changes with real data. A deployed system would ingest ambulance GPS traces, which are location data adjacent to patient information: health-data regulation, de-identification, access control and retention limits would apply before any real feed enters the twin. The signal side (queue counts from the control centre’s cameras) is operational data without personal content.
  • Ethics and safety. This is a research artefact. The learned rule is designed to be deployable behind an existing signal controller’s interlocks, as the proposal says, but nothing here drives a real signal: the safety shield (the plant of Section 5) is simulated, and a deployment would first need the real-data steps above. Priority shifts delay onto general traffic, so fairness across approaches is measured as the spread of mean car delay across the eight entry nodes (12.3) and reported next to the ambulance gain, so that the trade-off the proposal promises is a number, not a sentence; the plant’s starvation guard (Section 5), not the max-green rule, is what stops an approach starving: whatever the controller requests, an occupied approach gets a green within the 180 s guard plus one decision interval and the all-reds around it, and max_approach_red_s records the realised worst case per episode. The label rule is a published, inspectable formula. Generative-AI use is disclosed in 12.7, as the unit requires.

12.7 Use of generative AI (statement for the report)

The proposal’s statement is carried forward and widened to cover what has been produced since. Wording for the report, to be checked by every group member before submission:

“We used Claude (Anthropic, via Claude Code, September–November 2026) to brainstorm candidate framings, to critique our simulator design, to draft the simulator code, its unit tests, the dataset generator, the validation and modelling scripts, the digital-twin extension, the R Markdown demonstration and this methodology companion, all of which we reviewed, ran, tested and modified, to draft and revise the proposal and this report from our problem choice, design decisions and notes, and to check reference details by web search. The choice of problem, the design decisions and the cited sources are our own, and we re-checked every reference against its published version.”

13. Limitations and future work

No amber (replaced by stop-or-commit and an extended all-red); no lane changing (merge inside the box); split phasing, which lowers capacity relative to paired phasing; Poisson arrivals with a flat profile; IDM drivers without reaction time; no pedestrians or motorcycles; a box-empty clearance gate rather than a per-movement conflict matrix; free-flow time ignoring the turn slow-down; the box counted empty when a vehicle’s front bumper leaves it; no teacher-driven episodes in the behaviour mixture; no per-row ambulance-delay-ahead label.

Known properties of the specified rules, documented in the data card: the max-pressure teacher switches about four times a minute and loses to fixed time at high demand; hard braking near the stop-or-commit boundary occurs at 0.63 events per red onset in the design episode (Section 10, Experiment 3); the realised junction capacity is about 10% below the textbook formula, which is why demand is calibrated against the measured value; and the starvation guard bounds the wait for a green, not the wait of a lane head behind an exit lane blocked by spillback, which the liveness measurements of Section 4.3 record.

The demand calibration is single-junction, and on the 2×2 grid the nominal high level is over capacity for the max-pressure family: 11 of 17 high-demand max-pressure and ε-greedy episodes end with more than 380 vehicles in the network (median 399, maximum 512), against a mean of 68 (maximum 198) under fixed time at the same level. The learned controller, trained on that teacher, inherits the property, so its high-demand results describe an over-saturated grid.

After the release, a first lock-step twin was built on top of the dataset as an extension: a hidden ‘physical’ run of the simulator feeds noisy, delayed detectors (loops, a queue camera per edge with misses, dropped frames and a 1 s delivery delay); a state estimator rebuilds the same feature row as the dataset from those detectors alone; the trained sensor-feature model controls the lights from that row; and a drift monitor compares estimate and detectors. Over a 24-hour simulated day with the daily demand profile at design level it handled 45,416 vehicles with 0 gridlocks and 0 invariant violations, a mean queue-estimation error of 0.64 vehicles, and 27 stuck-camera events detected and recovered. An offline replay of a logged showcase episode through the same estimator tracks the true queues with a mean absolute error of 0.60 vehicles per edge. The ambulance channel is read without noise in the twin, as in the dataset.

Planned: the per-row ambulance-delay-ahead label (the extra seconds the nearest ambulance on an approach spends queued over the next 30 s, computed in the post-pass from a per-ambulance 1 Hz log); a live link to real detectors and ambulance GPS, the remaining part of a digital twin in the sense of Kušić et al. (2023); SUMO (Lopez et al., 2018) as an external validation backend; reinforcement learning after the course (Wei et al., 2019); GPS noise and delivery delay on the ambulance channel; and calibration to a real Jakarta intersection.

Appendix A. Worked numeric examples

  • Commit distance. v2/(2bstop)v^2 / (2 b_{stop}): 13.9 m/s → 32.2 m; 16.0 m/s → 42.7 m; 17.4 m/s (ambulance) → 50.5 m; 5 m/s → 4.2 m.
  • Box clearing time of a just-committed vehicle: tclear(v)=v/6+20.5/vt_{clear}(v) = v/6 + 20.5/v: 5 m/s → 4.9 s; 11.1 m/s → 3.7 s; 16 m/s → 3.9 s; an ambulance (17.4 m/s, 6.0 m long, 22 m to clear) → 4.2 s.
  • Capacity. cformula=1631×2×18/96=612c_{formula} = 1631 \times 2 \times 18 / 96 = 612 veh/h per two-lane approach; the fixed-time capacity the simulated junction actually realises, and against which the demand levels are calibrated, is c=549c = 549 veh/h (90% of the formula value, Section 9).
  • Design demand. λbase=0.7×549/1.18=326\lambda_{base} = 0.7 \times 549 / 1.18 = 326 veh/h per entry; eight entries give about 2,605 vehicle requests per hour on the grid.
  • Webster (1958) at design load. d1=96(1−18/96)2/(2(1−0.7⋅18/96))=36.5d_1 = 96 (1 - 18/96)^2 / (2 (1 - 0.7 \cdot 18/96)) = 36.5 s; the simulated single-junction value at x=0.7x = 0.7 was 43.8 s (total delay including entry queueing).
  • Storage. ⌊186/6.5⌋=28\lfloor 186 / 6.5 \rfloor = 28 vehicles per internal lane; ⌊143/6.5⌋=22\lfloor 143 / 6.5 \rfloor = 22 per stub lane.
  • Teacher threshold. An ambulance with three queued cars ahead of it needs tclear=4+lstartup+3hsatt_{clear} = 4 + l_{startup} + 3\, h_{sat}, about 12 s with the measured values; the teacher asks for its green when the ETA falls to that number, the naive rule 20 s out regardless of the queue.

Appendix B. Implementation notes: where the generator refines the written design

The generator follows the project’s design specification; these refinements were made while building it and are recorded so that the document describes what actually runs and how to read the data.

  • Decision instants exist only during green, starting 5 s after onset, so the forced codes 1 (min green) and 3 (all-red) never occur; only 0 (none), 2 (max green) and 4 (starvation guard) appear.
  • A vehicle that leaves a connector in a step is not integrated again by the edge loop of the same step (an earlier version advanced it an extra vΔtv\,\Delta t at every junction crossing).
  • signal_ticks carries down_n_* in addition to occupancy so that the label is recomputable from the row alone.
  • An exit is “blocked” per edge when, on any of its lanes, the last vehicle is queued (v<2v < 2 m/s) and its rear bumper leaves less than lveh+s0+1=7.5l_{veh} + s_0 + 1 = 7.5 m free at the lane start; a vehicle that is driving away does not block. A vehicle whose target lane is blocked treats the stop line as its leader only while it can still stop at bstopb_{stop}; past that point it enters the box anyway and, if it halts inside, is counted in n_box_blocked. An approach with all three exits blocked gets pressure −109-10^9.
  • The label picks ties by lowest index and, at max green, the highest-pressure other approach; the plant’s forced switch picks the largest vehicle count in rotation order. The label is the request, not the applied phase.
  • y_mp_action is computed on every row; y_q_total_t30 is read at the first whole second ≥t+30\ge t + 30 (decision instants can fall on half seconds), is NaN on tail and cool-down rows, and is also NaN when the episode ended early through gridlock.
  • The stop line is a zero-speed virtual leader at Le−2L_e - 2, so vehicles halt about 2 m before it and enter the box at LeL_e; the stop-or-commit evaluation runs at the decision instant before vehicles move.
  • Turn anticipation uses a 120 m zone and half the driver’s comfortable deceleration (the design specification said 60 m and the full bb); see Section 3.4.
  • A vehicle leaves the box when its front bumper passes the connector end; the clearance gate is therefore slightly optimistic by the time its rear needs.
  • A hard brake is counted only while the vehicle is moving (v>0v > 0).
  • The 300 m ambulance horizon never binds on this grid (edges are 143 m and 186 m long), so ev_present_a is true from the moment an ambulance enters the approach edge; between the stop line and the box edge it is still reported, with ev_dist_a = 0 and ev_eta_a = 0.
  • n_ambulances counts ambulance requests over the whole episode; the ev_mean_* KPIs use ambulances requested in the main period. Ambulances store alpha = 1.0.
  • At box entry a through or boundary-bound vehicle takes the exit lane with fewer vehicles, counting vehicles already on connectors to that lane; two vehicles released side by side that aim for the same exit lane zipper-merge at the box entry, which shows up as hard brakes.
  • episodes.csv has the extra health and liveness columns n_entry_queued_end, n_invariant_violations, vehicle_steps, gridlock_junction, max_approach_red_s (longest red faced by an occupied approach), max_total_wait_s, n_forced_starvation, n_emergency_brakes (IDM demanded more than the physical braking limit while moving), n_commit_revoked, n_merge_holds, merge_hard_stops, max_head_wait_s, spillback_lock, n_spillback_locks, spillback_lock_t and spillback_lock_junction. The car delay penalty is filled in by the generator from the paired no-ambulance run and is NaN when that run is skipped.
  • All plants start at phase N, green, t=0t = 0; under fixed time the four junctions run a synchronised cycle until all-red extensions desynchronise them.
  • The sensor copy obs_q_* is drawn on every decision row from the sensor stream; no controller reads it.
  • The configuration saved with the dataset records the formula capacity, the measured capacity and their ratio next to the calibrated base rates, so the demand levels of any release can be re-derived.

obs_q_N int16 veh sensor Binomial(q_a, 1-p_miss) + Poisson(p_miss/2), p_miss = sensor_noise_level; = q_a at 0

ev_present_N bool n/a ev an ambulance is on the approach edge from arm N within ev_horizon_m of the stop line (GPS channel, no noise)
ev_dist_N float32 m ev distance of the nearest ambulance to the stop line; -1 if none
ev_eta_N float32 s ev ev_dist / max(v_ambulance, 3 m/s); -1 if none
ev_q_ahead_N int16 veh ev queued vehicles in the ambulance’s lane ahead of it; -1 if none (input of the priority_mp teacher)
ev_present_E bool n/a ev an ambulance is on the approach edge from arm E within ev_horizon_m of the stop line (GPS channel, no noise)
ev_dist_E float32 m ev distance of the nearest ambulance to the stop line; -1 if none

ev_present_S bool n/a ev an ambulance is on the approach edge from arm S within ev_horizon_m of the stop line (GPS channel, no noise)

ev_eta_S float32 s ev ev_dist / max(v_ambulance, 3 m/s); -1 if none

ev_present_W bool n/a ev an ambulance is on the approach edge from arm W within ev_horizon_m of the stop line (GPS channel, no noise)

action_requested int8 n/a action phase requested by the driving controller
action_applied int8 n/a action phase in force after the plant’s filter (the pending phase when a switch was accepted)
forced int8 n/a action 0 none, 1 min_green, 2 max_green, 3 all_red, 4 starvation guard (an occupied approach had no green for starvation_s)
switched bool n/a action a switch (all-red) started at this instant
y_mp_action int8 n/a label request of the priority-aware teacher priority_mp recomputed from this row (label for imitation): the ambulance’s approach when ev_eta_a <= allred_min + startup lost time + ev_q_ahead_a x saturation headway, otherwise the max-pressure request; identical to the max-pressure request on every row without an ambulance
y_q_total_t30 float32 veh label q_total of this junction at the first whole second >= t+30 (junction_1hz)
